slides.title: Things your doctor wishes you'd just ask

slides.q: Is it normal for my poop to float?
slides.a: Usually, yes. Floating poop often just has more gas or water in it, which can happen after high-fiber foods or a change in diet. It's not a problem on its own. Worth seeing a doctor if it's consistently greasy, very foul-smelling, hard to flush, or comes with weight loss or diarrhea.

slides.q: Why do I pee so much when I'm cold?
slides.a: It's called cold diuresis. When you're cold, blood vessels in your skin narrow to hold in heat, pushing more blood toward your core. Your kidneys respond by filtering out extra fluid, so you need to pee more. It's harmless. Worth checking with a doctor if you're peeing a lot all the time or always thirsty.

slides.q: Is it normal to have hair around my nipples?
slides.a: Very normal, for all genders. Hair around the areola is common, and hormone changes from puberty, pregnancy, or birth control can make it darker or more noticeable. Trimming is the easiest fix, since plucking can irritate. Worth seeing a doctor if hair suddenly increases all over your body or your periods become irregular.

slides.q: Why do my joints crack so much?
slides.a: Usually it's harmless. Cracking often comes from gas bubbles popping in joint fluid or tendons sliding over bone. Studies haven't found that cracking your knuckles causes arthritis. If it doesn't hurt, you can ignore it. Worth seeing a doctor if cracking comes with pain, swelling, locking, or a joint that gives way.

slides.q: Why is my tongue white in the morning?
slides.a: A light white coating is common, especially after sleep. It's usually bacteria, dead cells, and food bits trapped between tiny bumps on your tongue. Brushing your tongue and drinking water usually clear it. Worth seeing a doctor or dentist if it doesn't go away after a couple of weeks, hurts, or forms patches you can't brush off.
